passages.original: Scipionem et Polybius et Rutilius hoc anno mortuum scribunt. ego neque his neque Valerio adsentior, his, quod censoribus M.PorcioL.ValerioL.Valerium principem senatus ipsum censorem lectum invenio, cum superioribus duobus lustris Africanus fuisset, quo vivo, nisi ut ille senatu moveretur, quam notam nemo memoriae prodidit, alius princeps in locum eius lectus non esset.
passages.english: Both Polybius and Rutilius write that Scipio died in this year. I agree neither with them nor with Valerius: with them, because I find that when Marcus Porcius and Lucius Valerius were censors, Lucius Valerius, himself one of the censors, was chosen as leader of the senate, although Africanus had been [leader] in the two preceding *lustra* [five-year censorial periods]; and while he was alive, unless he had been removed from the senate, a mark of disgrace that no one has recorded, another leader would not have been chosen in his place.
passages.notes: The run-together names (M.PorcioL.ValerioL.Valerium) are spacing errors in the scan for M. Porcio, L. Valerio, L. Valerium. 'Valerius' is Valerius Antias, as the following context shows.
